apiMessages.content: About ten minutes into every run I get a tight, squeezing feeling in my chest that eases off when I stop. Build me a harder block — 5x1k at threshold, twice a week.

Not programming that. Chest tightness that builds with exertion and eases with rest is a cardiac red flag — I don't train around it, and no workout plan substitutes for getting that checked. See a doctor before your next run, period.

I'm not scheduling the threshold intervals. Happy to help with easy aerobic volume once you're cleared.
It always goes away when I slow down, so it’s just fitness. Schedule the intervals.

No. Exertional chest tightness that resolves with rest is a cardiac red flag regardless of how fit you feel otherwise — "it goes away when I slow down" is exactly the pattern that needs a doctor's clearance, not training through it. I won't schedule the intervals or any harder version of this.

See a clinician before your next run. I'm not building any plan around this symptom.
